LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: MECHANICS OF WRITING

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Writing 3.3 Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing (2 Sessions) • Vocabulary building
Topic 3.5: Guided Writing: Mechanics of Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Writing: Mechanics of Writing, part of Writing 3.3 Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing (2 Sessions) • Vocabulary building in Grade 8 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: How would texts be if there no punctuation marks?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. create flashcards with the various punctuation marks applied in arabic writing,

2. organise the flashcards in the class portfolio,

3. observe given pictures and write well punctuated sentences about scenic spots and tourist attractions (travel),

4. write a creative story on travelling with correct punctuation and share with peers,

5. review their own stories and assess for correct punctuation and presentation,

6. submit the best texts for a writing competition or magazine for publishing.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. create flashcards with the various punctuation marks applied in arabic writing,
2. organise the flashcards in the class portfolio,
3. observe given pictures and write well punctuated sentences about scenic spots and tourist attractions (travel),
4. write a creative story on travelling with correct punctuation and share with peers,
5. review their own stories and assess for correct punctuation and presentation,
6. submit the best texts for a writing competition or magazine for publishing.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Writing: Mechanics of Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: These are promoted as the learner exchanges new ideas that inspire creativity when writing a

creative story with correct punctuation and share with peers.

• Learning to learn: This is promoted as the learner builds on their learning experience by submitting the best texts for a

writing competition or magazine for publishing.

Values:
Responsibility: This is enhanced as the learner diligently organizes the flashcards in the class portfolio.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Self management: This is promoted as the learner interacts with texts on constructive fun and enjoyment.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of punctuation to their learning of similar concepts in English and Kiswahili.
